name: Machhi No Saas
subtitle: pomfret poached in a pale sweet-sour sauce thickened with egg and rice flour

ingredients.qty: 600g pomfret or seer, cut into 4 steaks

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with salt and a squeeze of the vinegar and leave 20 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Grind the garlic, green chilli, cumin seeds and ginger to a fine paste with 2 tbsp water before you start cooking.
Slake the rice flour in 4 tbsp cold water and keep it beside the stove. Added dry it will lump instantly.

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the onion gently until soft and translucent but not coloured, 8 minutes.
steps.tip: Saas is a pale sauce. Brown onion here and it will look and taste wrong.

steps.text: Add the ground garlic-chilli-cumin paste and fry 2 minutes, until it stops smelling raw.
Pour in the water with salt, bring to a simmer, and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the slaked rice flour and simmer 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon lightly.
Slide in the fish steaks in a single layer and poach on low 8-10 minutes, spooning sauce over rather than turning them.
steps.tip: Turning breaks the steaks. Baste instead.

steps.text: Lift the fish out onto a serving dish and keep it warm.
Beat the eggs with the vinegar until smooth.
Take the pan off the heat, wait a minute, then trickle in the egg-vinegar mixture in a thin stream while whisking hard.
steps.tip: Off the heat and slowly. Straight into a boiling pan the egg scrambles and the sauce is ruined.

steps.text: Return to the lowest heat with the sugar and stir 2 minutes until the sauce thickens to a thin custard. It must not boil.
Taste for the sweet-sour balance, pour over the fish, scatter with coriander and serve with plain boiled rice.

storage: Eat the same day. Refrigerated it keeps 1 day; reheat over the gentlest heat or in a bain-marie, as a boil will split the egg-thickened sauce.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
